title: Mexican Rice
subtitle: Tomato rice with cumin, garlic, and chicken stock
excerpt: Long-grain rice toasted in oil until golden, then simmered in seasoned tinned tomatoes and chicken stock with garlic and cumin until fluffy and full of flavour. The standard Tex-Mex side dish and burrito filling.
sourceNotes: Mexican rice (arroz rojo / Spanish rice): a Tex-Mex and northern Mexican rice dish made by toasting rice in oil before simmering in tomato broth. Toasting gives the rice a nutty flavour and prevents it going sticky. A staple side dish in Tex-Mex restaurants and homes since the 1960s. Based on classic American and Mexican Tex-Mex published sources.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freezes well for up to 3 months. Defrost overnight in the fridge and reheat in a pan with a splash of water.
recipe.batchNotes: Double the batch; reheats perfectly for the rest of the week.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make ahead and refrigerate for up to 3 days. Reheat covered in the microwave or in a pan with a little water.

content.text: Mexican rice gets its character from two things: toasting the dry rice in oil before any liquid goes in, and using a mixture of tinned tomatoes and stock as the cooking liquid. Toasting the raw rice in oil until golden gives the grains a nutty flavour and a light coating that keeps them separate during cooking. Don't skip this step. Measure the liquid carefully; too much and the rice goes mushy, too little and it's undercooked.

items.prepNote: rinsed until the water runs clear, then drained

content.text: The total liquid is 600 ml: 200 ml blended tomatoes + 400 ml stock. This gives a 2:1 liquid-to-rice ratio for long-grain rice.

Heat {{vegetable-oil}} of oil in a medium saucepan over medium heat. Add the rinsed and drained rice. Cook, stirring regularly, for 4-5 minutes until the grains turn pale golden and smell nutty. Don't rush this step.
Add {{onion}} of finely chopped onion. Cook for 2 minutes. Add {{garlic}} of crushed garlic, the cumin, and chilli powder. Cook for 1 minute.

Pour in the blended tinned tomatoes and the chicken stock. Season with salt. Bring to a simmer, stirring once. Reduce to the lowest heat, put on a tight-fitting lid, and cook for 18 minutes without lifting the lid.
Remove from the heat. Leave with the lid on for 5 minutes to steam. Fluff with a fork. Taste and adjust seasoning. Scatter with coriander if using.

items.cause: Too much liquid, or lid lifted during cooking releasing steam
items.fix: Measure the liquid carefully: 200ml tomato + 400ml stock is exact. Don't lift the lid during cooking. If already mushy, spread on a baking tray and put in a warm oven for 10 minutes to dry out.

items.symptom: Rice has a firm, undercooked core
items.cause: Not enough liquid, or cooked on too high a heat
items.fix: Add 50 ml more stock, replace the lid, and cook for 5 more minutes. The heat must be at its lowest setting; too much heat cooks off the liquid before the rice is done.

items.symptom: Rice has no colour and tastes bland
items.cause: Toasting step skipped or cut short
items.fix: The golden toasting stage is essential for flavour. Cook the dry rice in the oil, stirring, until every grain looks pale gold and smells toasted.

items.symptom: Tomato flavour too strong and paste-like
items.cause: Whole tinned tomatoes blended without diluting
items.fix: Blend only half a tin (200ml) and dilute with 400ml stock. Full-tin tomato-forward rice tastes more like a risotto than Mexican rice.

content.text: Mexican rice, also called arroz rojo or Spanish rice in American Tex-Mex usage, is a side dish found across northern Mexico and the US Tex-Mex tradition. It appears alongside refried beans on nearly every combination plate in a Tex-Mex restaurant. Toasting raw rice in fat before adding liquid is used across Spanish, Mexican, and Middle Eastern cooking. It produces a far better texture than adding dry rice straight to liquid.
